title: Intellectual Property Licensing — Operator Companion Workbook
subtitle: 6 Printable Operator Worksheets for Patent, Brand, Catalog, and Dataset Licensing: Rights Underwriting, Minimum Guarantees, Royalty Controls, Contract Execution, Automation, and Transfer-Ready Operations

worksheets.title: Opportunity Underwriting and Licensee Qualification
worksheets.purpose: Select a licensable asset and solvent counterparty before spending on prosecution, packaging, or negotiations. Establish ownership, commercial demand, permitted uses, territorial boundaries, and reporting feasibility. Convert speculative intellectual property into an evidence-backed deal thesis with explicit rejection criteria.
instructions: Create one underwriting record per asset and proposed licensee. Separate patents, brands, copyrighted catalogs, and datasets because their ownership evidence and permissible uses differ. Attach dated source documents rather than relying on a seller's presentation.

Interview product, procurement, and accounting personnel at the prospective licensee. Confirm the product roadmap, budget owner, launch timing, and royalty-reporting system. Treat enthusiastic technical feedback without purchasing authority as discovery evidence, not committed demand.

Map the proposed grant across territory, field of use, channels, term, exclusivity, and sublicensing. Test each dimension against existing grants and retained rights. Identify overlaps before discussing a price or promising category exclusivity.

Calculate operator revenue separately from licensee product sales. Use the canonical annual scenarios as portfolio reference points, then document the commercial assumptions supporting this particular deal. Reject projections that quietly count the licensee's manufacturing turnover as licensing revenue.

Assign an owner and resolution date to every material uncertainty. Rank evidence by source quality and commercial consequence. Advance only when title, demand, solvency, and reporting capability are documented sufficiently to justify the next underwriting expenditure.

fields.name: Asset identity and monetizable advantage
fields.prompt: Identify the specific asset, protected subject matter, customer problem, and measurable advantage. Explain why a licensee would pay instead of building, sourcing, or using a substitute with fewer restrictions.
fields.example: A catalog contains 240 commissioned industrial illustrations with signed assignments and editable source files. Four equipment publishers need consistent maintenance diagrams. The proposed license replaces an estimated 600 annual illustration hours per publisher; the underwriting record links that estimate to two procurement interviews and three recent production invoices.

fields.name: Chain of title and encumbrance evidence
fields.prompt: List creators, inventors, employers, assignors, registration references, and prior grants. Identify liens, retained rights, termination interests, or missing signatures that could prevent the exact license proposed to this counterparty.
fields.example: The asset register links 240 illustration files to eight creator agreements and eight signed assignments. Two agreements reserve portfolio-display rights but no commercial sublicensing rights. The operator obtains a seller lien search and releases before closing; 12 illustrations with incomplete assignment schedules remain excluded from the initial licensed catalog.

fields.name: Buyer problem and verified demand
fields.prompt: Record who experiences the problem, who controls purchasing, and what evidence supports willingness to pay. Distinguish interviews, sample evaluations, budget reservations, and executed purchase commitments rather than blending them into one pipeline total.
fields.example: Discovery covers 12 publishers: seven confirm a diagram backlog, four accept a sample package, and two budget owners discuss annual licensing. One procurement manager confirms a $110,000 spending envelope by email. No interview enters booked revenue; the next milestone is a signed paid evaluation with defined conversion terms.

fields.name: Counterparty solvency and payment security
fields.prompt: Document the contracting entity, payment history, available credit evidence, and exposure before collection. Specify when deposits, parent support, shorter reporting intervals, or restricted delivery are necessary for a newly formed or thinly capitalized licensee.
fields.example: The proposed licensee is a recently formed subsidiary with $85,000 cash and no trading history. The operator requires a $15,000 quarterly minimum payment before access, a parent guarantee reviewed for enforceability, and monthly sales reports. Source-file delivery waits until the first payment clears and the authorized signatory is verified.

fields.name: Territory, field, channel, and exclusivity
fields.prompt: Define the grant using boundaries that operations can enforce. State included products, excluded applications, geographic coverage, sales channels, affiliates, sublicense permissions, and performance conditions for retaining any negotiated exclusivity.
fields.example: The grant covers maintenance manuals for commercial refrigeration equipment sold in the United States and Canada for 24 months. Consumer appliances, merchandise, and training-model use are excluded. Exclusivity applies only to the named refrigeration field and converts to nonexclusive status if the annual $60,000 minimum is not paid after the contractual cure period.

fields.name: Competitive substitutes and infringement exposure
fields.prompt: Identify competing assets, public-domain alternatives, technical workarounds, and plausible infringement allegations. Separate ownership of the offered asset from the licensee's freedom to commercialize a finished product containing other protected components.
fields.example: A sensor patent license covers one calibration method, not the entire device. The licensee identifies three competing calibration methods and commissions a separate product clearance review. The operator supplies claim charts and prosecution records; the proposal does not represent that the license automatically clears enclosure, wireless, or firmware rights.

fields.name: Royalty data availability and audit access
fields.prompt: Verify that the licensee can produce transaction-level records matching the proposed royalty definition. Specify identifiers, deduction evidence, affiliate transfers, returns, currency treatment, retention periods, and an achievable contractual inspection mechanism.
fields.example: The licensee exports invoice ID, SKU, territory, gross sales, returns, freight, tax, and currency from NetSuite. The draft permits documented returns and separately stated sales tax as deductions, but excludes general overhead. A seven-year record retention clause and annual independent inspection right support reconciliation back to the sales ledger.

fields.name: Portfolio revenue thesis and scenario anchor
fields.prompt: Select the canonical scenario used for planning and explain the revenue composition. Show underlying licensee sales only as a royalty driver, with license fees and earned royalties reported separately as operator revenue.
fields.example: The Base portfolio targets $425,000 annual operator revenue: $125,000 nonrecoupable license fees plus $300,000 earned royalties. At a 5% royalty rate, those royalties require $6,000,000 eligible licensee sales. Four equal accounts contribute $106,250 operator revenue each; the $6,000,000 sales denominator never appears as operator gross revenue.

fields.name: Underwriting budget and decision timetable
fields.prompt: Set a staged expenditure limit for title review, demand testing, valuation, and negotiation. Connect spending releases to evidence received, and distinguish the 30-day preparation sprint from the likely time needed to close a first license.
fields.example: The operator starts with $75,000 capital, within the $25,000 to $250,000 planning range. Initial underwriting receives $9,000: $4,000 title work, $2,500 customer testing, and $2,500 contract design. A further $6,000 requires two qualified licensees. The first-deal planning window remains 4 to 14 months, not the first sprint.

fields.name: Advance, revise, or reject decision
fields.prompt: Record the decision, decisive evidence, unresolved issues, and next expenditure limit. Make rejection criteria observable so commercial enthusiasm cannot override defective title, absent purchasing authority, or an unauditable royalty calculation.
fields.example: Decision: revise before negotiation. Demand and budget are credible, but 12 catalog assets lack complete assignment schedules and the buyer cannot yet report affiliate sales. The operator excludes those assets, requests an affiliate export within ten business days, and caps additional diligence at $2,000 until both issues are resolved.

worksheets.completion_gate: The deal owner signs a dated decision supported by a rights map, buyer evidence, solvency review, auditable royalty definition, and bounded diligence budget; unresolved rights are excluded explicitly.

worksheets.title: Unit Economics, Defect Reserve, and Working-Capital Float
worksheets.purpose: Reconcile license-level economics to the three canonical annual scenarios without counting customer product sales as operator revenue. Model minimum guarantees, recoupment, collection timing, defect exposure, and liquidity separately so strong contracted royalties do not conceal a near-term cash shortage.
instructions: Copy the canonical revenue, margin, owner profit, and staffing figures into the scenario record before building supporting assumptions. Derive total annual costs by subtraction. Keep monthly fixed overhead distinct from the broader annual cost envelope.

Write the royalty formula using the agreement's eligible sales definition, permitted deductions, currency rules, and reporting periods. Model recoupable minimums as credits against the same earned royalties, never as additional revenue automatically stacked above them.

Prepare separate earned-revenue, invoicing, and cash schedules. A payment date alone does not establish revenue recognition. Document the accounting treatment of each license fee, access obligation, support service, and annual minimum with the accounting owner.

Build a managerial reserve for refunds, title defects, collection disputes, and reporting corrections using explicit probability and exposure assumptions. Identify whether each amount is already inside the scenario cost envelope to prevent duplicate deductions.

Stress collection delays and lower sales independently. Show opening cash, restricted amounts, overdue receivables, and the minimum operating buffer by month. Escalate when unrestricted cash cannot cover the next committed payments without assuming an unsigned deal closes.

fields.name: Canonical annual scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Enter all three canonical annual cases with revenue, net margin, owner net profit, total costs, and staffing. Use exact amounts so every supporting worksheet can reconcile to the same portfolio baseline.
fields.example: Conservative: $50,000 revenue, 25% margin, $12,500 owner net, $37,500 costs, 1 FT plus 3 C. Base: $425,000 revenue, 42.5% margin, $180,625 owner net, $244,375 costs, same staffing. Scaled: $800,000 revenue, 60% margin, $480,000 owner net, $320,000 costs, 2 FT plus 4 C.

fields.name: License fees and royalty revenue bridge
fields.prompt: Specify a nonoverlapping revenue composition for each scenario. State the royalty rate and eligible sales denominator, and identify the treatment of nonrecoupable fees separately from royalty advances and minimum guarantees.
fields.example: Conservative combines $20,000 fees with $30,000 royalties on $600,000 eligible sales. Base combines $125,000 fees with $300,000 royalties on $6,000,000 sales. Scaled combines $200,000 fees with $600,000 royalties on $12,000,000 sales. All three use 5%; modeled fees are nonrecoupable and recognized within the illustrated annual period.

fields.name: Minimum guarantee and recoupment waterfall
fields.prompt: Define the minimum payment, payment dates, recoupment pool, carryforward rules, and true-up sequence. Show why the guarantee protects a floor without being counted twice when earned royalties exceed that floor.
fields.example: Each Base licensee owes a $60,000 annual minimum against earned royalties, paid in four $15,000 installments. At $1,500,000 annual eligible sales, earned royalties equal $75,000. The licensee pays a further $15,000 true-up; royalty revenue is $75,000, not $135,000. Credits expire annually and cannot cross between licensees.

fields.name: Quarterly royalty calculation and deductions
fields.prompt: Calculate one reporting period from gross transactions through eligible sales, earned royalties, minimum credits, and balance due. Give each deduction a contractual basis and preserve the supporting source-record reference.
fields.example: Across four Base accounts, quarterly gross sales are $1,575,000. Documented returns of $45,000 and separately stated sales tax of $30,000 produce $1,500,000 eligible sales. At 5%, earned royalties are $75,000. Quarterly minimum payments total $60,000, leaving $15,000 additional royalties due without subtracting unrelated marketing expenses.

fields.name: Annual costs and monthly overhead boundary
fields.prompt: Separate recurring fixed overhead from other annual operating costs. Reconcile both categories to canonical profit, and explain why total annual costs divided by twelve need not equal the stated fixed-overhead planning range.
fields.example: Conservative uses $24,000 fixed overhead plus $13,500 other costs. Base uses $96,000 plus $148,375. Scaled uses $180,000 plus $140,000. Fixed monthly overhead is therefore $2,000, $8,000, and $15,000. Other costs include deal-specific support, outside specialists, and forecast losses, without changing the canonical annual net figures.

fields.name: Scrub and title-defect reserve
fields.prompt: Estimate the managerial reserve for defective rights, disputed deductions, refunds, and collection loss. Separate expected economic exposure from accounting entries, and show its position inside the existing annual scenario cost envelope.
fields.example: The Base plan allocates $12,000 within its $148,375 other-cost envelope: $6,000 for reporting adjustments, $4,000 for title-remediation work, and $2,000 for collection losses. This planning reserve is not an automatic ledger expense. Recognized provisions and actual costs follow the accounting policy; the model never deducts the reserve twice.

fields.name: Opening capital and collection-delay float
fields.prompt: Build a cash bridge using actual receipt dates and committed outflows rather than annual profit averages. Identify minimum liquidity, collection timing sensitivity, and which discretionary expenditures can pause without breaching contracts.
fields.example: Opening capital of $75,000 funds $25,000 setup work, leaving $50,000 unrestricted cash. Three months of $8,000 fixed overhead and a $10,000 specialist payment leave $16,000 before receipts. A further month without collection reduces cash to $8,000, below the chosen $16,000 two-month fixed-overhead buffer.

fields.name: Revenue recognition and deferred cash
fields.prompt: Identify the performance obligations and recognition policy for fees, royalties, support, and advance payments. Reconcile cash received with earned revenue and deferred balances, including the evidence supporting any point-in-time treatment.
fields.example: A licensee pays its $31,250 nonrecoupable fee and first $15,000 minimum together, producing $46,250 cash. The accounting owner documents when the specific license is available for use and whether continuing obligations alter recognition. The annual Base model assumes $31,250 fee revenue and $75,000 royalties, not immediate recognition of every receipt.

fields.name: Downside sensitivity and guarantee exposure
fields.prompt: Model lower licensee sales and collection failure separately from the canonical cases. State which minimum obligations remain enforceable and collectible, and keep sensitivities clearly labeled rather than silently replacing published scenario figures.
fields.example: In a Base sensitivity, eligible sales fall 30% to $4,200,000, producing $210,000 percentage royalties. Collectible annual minimums of $240,000 establish the modeled royalty floor. With unchanged $125,000 fees and $244,375 costs, illustrative revenue becomes $365,000 and owner net $120,625; the canonical Base remains $425,000 and $180,625.

fields.name: Capital allocation and payout discipline
fields.prompt: Set rules for owner distributions, reserve replenishment, and new asset acquisition. Tie available cash to collected receivables and committed obligations rather than treating forecast owner profit as immediately distributable money.
fields.example: The operator withholds distributions while unrestricted cash is below $16,000 or a material title claim remains unfunded. A proposed $20,000 catalog acquisition requires a separate cash forecast including specialist invoices and the next minimum-payment cycle. Base annual owner net stays $180,625, but payment timing follows actual liquidity and entity-level obligations.

worksheets.completion_gate: The accounting owner verifies all three exact scenario reconciliations, the minimum-credit waterfall, reserve placement, and a dated cash forecast showing the lowest unrestricted balance and required response.

worksheets.title: Execution Ledger and Technical QA Pre-Flight
worksheets.purpose: Translate signed rights into controlled delivery, accurate royalty statements, and reproducible audit evidence. Define identifiers, source records, calculation versions, access controls, and exception handling before the first reporting cycle, with distinct technical checks for patent, brand, catalog, and dataset licenses.
instructions: Create persistent identifiers for the agreement, amendment, asset, licensee, reporting period, statement, and receipt. Use those identifiers across the contract repository and ledger so an auditor can trace one royalty amount without relying on filenames alone.

Convert every operative clause into a named obligation with a responsible person, due date, evidence requirement, and escalation path. Include delivery, marking, quality review, sublicensing, reporting, payment, renewal, and post-termination duties.

Run a pre-delivery rights and technical review against the executed asset schedule. Compare file hashes, territorial permissions, approved branding, dataset provenance, and access permissions. Quarantine mismatches instead of expanding the grant through an informal delivery.

Recompute the first royalty statement independently from transaction records. Test duplicates, missing identifiers, reversed invoices, currencies, deductions, and minimum-credit allocation. Preserve both the original submission and the corrected version with an explanation of every change.

Close the period only after ledger totals, invoices, receipts, and exception records reconcile. Retain the calculation version and reviewer evidence. An unresolved discrepancy must have an owner, bounded amount, next action, and contractual deadline.

fields.name: Agreement and asset identifier register
fields.prompt: Define stable identifiers and relationships connecting each asset to its executed grant, amendments, licensee entity, and reporting obligations. Prevent informal project names from becoming the sole reference for enforceable rights.
fields.example: Agreement LIC-013-004 connects entity PUB-004 to catalog CAT-240, asset schedule version 3, and amendment AMD-001. The executed schedule contains 228 deliverable illustrations after excluding 12 incomplete-title items. Each illustration retains its own asset ID, checksum, creator agreement reference, permitted territory, and approved distribution format.

fields.name: Clause-to-obligation execution ledger
fields.prompt: Extract operational duties from the executed agreement and assign evidence-based completion criteria. Include contractual cure periods and notices so a missed internal reminder does not become an invented termination right.
fields.example: Clause 6.2 requires quarterly statements within 30 days after quarter-end; clause 6.3 requires payment within the same period. The royalty analyst prepares the reconciliation, the operator reviews it, and the ledger stores delivery evidence. Late-payment notices follow the negotiated ten-business-day cure mechanism and designated notice addresses.

fields.name: Catalog and dataset delivery manifest
fields.prompt: Specify deliverable versions, integrity checks, source permissions, access limitations, and acceptance tests. For datasets, include provenance, permitted transformations, prohibited uses, and the contractual treatment of updates and derived outputs.
fields.example: A dataset delivery contains 80,000 equipment observations in CSV files, a schema dictionary, and a SHA-256 manifest. Validation confirms row counts, permitted source licenses, and removal of direct personal identifiers. The grant allows internal predictive maintenance analysis but excludes resale and model training unless a signed amendment adds those uses.

fields.name: Brand quality and patent-use pre-flight
fields.prompt: List asset-specific checks beyond file delivery, including brand quality controls, approved specimens, patent claim scope, marking instructions, and responsibility for finished-product clearance outside the licensed rights.
fields.example: A brand license requires review of packaging artwork and two production samples before sale, with defects logged against the quality schedule. A separate patent license identifies covered claims and any applicable marking instructions under 35 U.S.C. § 287(a). Neither workflow treats an approved logo or patent grant as product-wide clearance.

fields.name: Source data schema and ingestion controls
fields.prompt: Define required columns, accepted formats, identifier uniqueness, period rules, and rejection behavior. State how the operator preserves raw submissions while converting licensee-specific exports into a consistent royalty calculation dataset.
fields.example: The ingestion schema requires licensee_id, invoice_id, line_id, SKU, invoice_date, territory, currency, gross_amount, return_amount, and tax_amount. A composite licensee-invoice-line key rejects duplicates. Raw CSV files remain immutable in a restricted S3 bucket; normalized records enter a separate ledger with import timestamp, source checksum, and validation results.

fields.name: Royalty calculation acceptance tests
fields.prompt: Write test cases with expected outputs for deductions, returns, rates, rounding, currencies, and recoupment. Include failure cases that must stop statement generation rather than producing plausible but unreviewed royalty totals.
fields.example: A $10,000 sale with $500 permitted returns yields $9,500 eligible sales and $475 royalty at 5%. A duplicate invoice line must fail ingestion. An unapproved 8% marketing deduction must be rejected. Portfolio quarterly royalties of $75,000 less $60,000 minimum credits must produce exactly $15,000 additional royalties due.

fields.name: Statement, receivable, and receipt reconciliation
fields.prompt: Connect earned royalties to statements, invoices, credits, bank receipts, and outstanding balances. Distinguish a missing payment from a disputed calculation and preserve the cash-application rule for partial or combined remittances.
fields.example: Statement STM-Q1-004 records $18,750 earned royalties for one Base account. The ledger applies its $15,000 quarterly minimum receipt, leaving $3,750 due. A $3,000 remittance reduces the receivable to $750. The operator records the short payment without rewriting earned royalties or allocating another licensee's available credit.

fields.name: Royalty audit sampling and discrepancy treatment
fields.prompt: Define the population, sampling method, escalation threshold, and evidence required to expand testing. Specify how contractual audit-cost shifting, interest, and corrections are calculated without assuming every discrepancy proves intentional concealment.
fields.example: An audit reconciles the full SKU list and samples 40 invoices across territories and channels. Testing finds $200,000 eligible sales omitted from a separate audit-period submission, implying $10,000 underpaid royalties at 5%. The auditor expands testing, evaluates the contract's cost-shifting threshold, and records any recovery outside the unchanged canonical baseline.

fields.name: Exception ownership and correction history
fields.prompt: Record the issue, affected amount, source evidence, owner, deadline, and resolution authority. Preserve superseded statements and calculation versions so a correction remains explainable during a later audit or portfolio sale.
fields.example: Exception EX-017 concerns $45,000 returns deducted without credit-memo references. The analyst requests support within five business days and freezes only the disputed adjustment. Version 1 remains archived; version 2 records $30,000 supported returns and a $750 royalty increase on the unsupported $15,000 balance at 5%.

fields.name: Termination, access withdrawal, and retention
fields.prompt: Translate expiration and termination provisions into technical actions while preserving required evidence. Address credentials, delivered copies, sell-off rights, final statements, retained backups, and the boundaries of any continuing access permission.
fields.example: After the contractual cure period expires, the operator sends the required notice and disables future dataset downloads on the effective termination date. A negotiated 60-day inventory sell-off remains reportable and royalty-bearing. The licensee certifies deletion of prohibited working copies while the operator retains contracts and accounting evidence under the seven-year records schedule.

worksheets.completion_gate: A reviewer reproduces one complete royalty statement from preserved source records, confirms delivery against the executed grant, and signs the exception ledger with every material discrepancy resolved or bounded.

worksheets.title: Statutory, Contract, Licensing, and Outreach Audit
worksheets.purpose: Identify the concrete statutory and contractual requirements governing the proposed asset and sales motion. Link each requirement to documents, operating controls, and accountable reviewers, while separating ownership, permitted use, privacy, competition, and outreach questions that cannot be resolved by one broad warranty.
instructions: Classify each licensed component before reviewing the agreement. A product package can contain patents, marks, copyrighted files, confidential know-how, and personal data simultaneously. Create separate evidence requirements instead of assuming one registration establishes rights in every component.

Check ownership documents against the precise grant and applicable statutory requirements. Record jurisdiction, effective dates, signatures, recording status, and retained interests. Route material gaps to the assigned specialist before promising exclusivity or unrestricted sublicensing.

Review royalty definitions alongside competition, territorial, and duration provisions. Flag arrangements involving price coordination, market allocation, coercive bundles, or patent-expiration issues for fact-specific review. Do not treat a standard template as a substantive assessment.

Map data flows and outreach channels separately from intellectual-property ownership. Establish processing purposes, recipient restrictions, suppression handling, and evidence retention. A license to use a database does not automatically authorize every personal-data use or marketing contact.

Close each audit item with a document reference, control owner, and retest date. Track contractual deviations in the obligation ledger so negotiated protections survive handoff to the royalty analyst, delivery contractor, and commercial relationship owner.

fields.name: Patent ownership and territorial coverage
fields.prompt: Identify issued claims, jurisdictions, expiration assumptions, maintenance status, assignments, and prior licenses. Connect the proposed grant to actual patent rights rather than application titles or marketing descriptions of worldwide protection.
fields.example: The patent file includes signed assignments under 35 U.S.C. § 261, USPTO recording references, maintenance-fee records, and claim charts for two issued United States patents. A pending European application is labeled separately. The contract grants only listed rights and requires updates if claims lapse, expire, or materially change during the term.

fields.name: Patent expiration, exhaustion, and marking
fields.prompt: Review royalty duration, authorized sales, downstream restrictions, and applicable marking duties. Separate current patent use from deferred payment, know-how rights, and other consideration when constructing a royalty schedule extending beyond patent expiration.
fields.example: A patent expires in year three of a five-year commercial relationship. The draft separates patent consideration from continuing know-how support and reviews Brulotte v. Thys and Kimble v. Marvel before setting later payments. Product marking is assessed under 35 U.S.C. § 287(a); authorized-sale effects are reviewed under Impression Products v. Lexmark.

fields.name: Copyright transfers and catalog permissions
fields.prompt: Verify signed transfers, work-made-for-hire assumptions, underlying components, and reserved rights for catalog assets. Review termination interests and distinguish copyright in selection or arrangement from rights in individual facts or third-party material.
fields.example: For 240 illustrations, the operator checks written transfers under 17 U.S.C. § 204(a) and evaluates work-made-for-hire claims under § 101. Older author grants receive termination review under §§ 203 and 304 where applicable. Stock photographs embedded in 18 files require separate redistribution permission before inclusion in the deliverable schedule.

fields.name: Trademark ownership and quality controls
fields.prompt: Record mark ownership, covered goods, territorial registrations, quality standards, inspection rights, and corrective actions. Distinguish a license from an assignment and ensure practical oversight supports the continuing significance of the licensed mark.
fields.example: The brand schedule identifies registered marks, approved refrigeration products, and packaging specimens. Quality reviews occur before launch and quarterly thereafter, with documented correction rights. The review considers abandonment principles in 15 U.S.C. § 1127; any proposed ownership transfer separately addresses the goodwill requirements of 15 U.S.C. § 1060.

fields.name: Dataset rights, privacy, and purpose limits
fields.prompt: Separate source permissions, confidentiality, copyright, database restrictions, and personal-data obligations. Record processing purposes and recipient roles, and avoid treating a purchased collection of facts as unrestricted ownership of every downstream use.
fields.example: A maintenance dataset contains 80,000 observations plus technician identifiers. The operator removes unnecessary identifiers and documents source permissions. Review addresses 17 U.S.C. §§ 102(b) and 103, applicable California Civil Code § 1798.100 duties, and GDPR Articles 6, 28, and 44 when relevant. Model-training rights require an express purpose assessment and contractual grant.

fields.name: Trade-secret handling and disclosure controls
fields.prompt: Identify confidential know-how that derives value from secrecy and define reasonable protection measures. Specify recipient access, onward disclosure, return duties, incident notice, and evidence proving the information was treated as confidential.
fields.example: A calibration recipe is distributed only to three named engineers through role-restricted access. The agreement bars unauthorized disclosure and requires return or deletion after termination. The operator logs access and labels the technical package confidential, supporting the reasonable-measures element of 18 U.S.C. § 1839(3) rather than relying on secrecy language alone.

fields.name: Competition constraints and exclusivity review
fields.prompt: Assess commercial context for exclusivity, territorial limits, tying, grantbacks, resale restrictions, and competitor coordination. Record market facts and rationale so a specialist can evaluate the actual arrangement rather than a clause in isolation.
fields.example: A proposed exclusive refrigeration-field license runs 24 months and depends on a $60,000 annual minimum. The operator documents substitute suppliers, market position, and investment rationale. Review addresses Sherman Act §§ 1 and 2, 15 U.S.C. §§ 1 and 2, and applicable Clayton Act § 3 issues under 15 U.S.C. § 14.

fields.name: Royalty definitions and dispute mechanics
fields.prompt: Audit the contract's economic language for inconsistent definitions, ambiguous deductions, affiliate leakage, and inaccessible evidence. Specify reporting deadlines, audit procedures, correction mechanics, remedies, and notice requirements in executable operational terms.
fields.example: Eligible sales exclude documented returns and separately stated sales tax, but not internal commissions. Affiliate transfers use the expressly defined valuation method. Statements and payments are due 30 days after quarter-end. The agreement provides annual inspection on 20 business days' notice and shifts reasonable audit costs when underpayment exceeds 5% of royalties due.

fields.name: Commercial outreach and suppression controls
fields.prompt: Document the actual email, telephone, and messaging channels used for licensee acquisition. Connect applicable requirements to sender identity, address information, opt-out processing, calling permissions, and records showing suppression before subsequent campaigns.
fields.example: The initial campaign uses individually reviewed commercial email to 40 business contacts. Templates include accurate routing information, required advertising identification, a physical postal address, and functioning opt-out instructions under 15 U.S.C. § 7704. The operator honors opt-outs within ten business days; automated calls and texts require separate 47 U.S.C. § 227 review.

fields.name: Contract authority, jurisdiction, and exceptions
fields.prompt: Verify signatory authority, governing law, dispute forum, notice addresses, assignment restrictions, and cross-border payment requirements. Capture deviations from the approved commercial position with their operational consequence and designated reviewer.
fields.example: The subsidiary's procurement manager provides delegated signing authority, while the parent guarantee receives a separate authorized signature. The contract specifies governing law, forum, and notice delivery methods. A negotiated assignment restriction requires consent for an asset sale; the exit ledger flags that dependency before the operator markets the portfolio.

worksheets.completion_gate: The assigned reviewers close the rights, privacy, competition, contract, and outreach checks with cited evidence; each remaining restriction is reflected in the grant, delivery controls, and obligation ledger.

worksheets.title: Automation, Growth Flywheel, and Risk Fallback Tracker
worksheets.purpose: Automate repetitive royalty administration without surrendering control of contractual interpretation, cash application, or sensitive data. Build a narrow outbound engine around verified buyer needs, then define observable failure signals and manual fallback procedures for reporting, renewals, delivery, and disputes.
instructions: Start with the three named automation levers: royalty reporting, license renewal alerts, and contract obligation tracking. Assign each workflow a source of truth, service owner, reconciliation test, and manual procedure before connecting production data.

Separate deterministic calculations from interpretive decisions. Software may validate schemas, calculate approved rates, and schedule reminders. A responsible person resolves ambiguous grant language, disputed deductions, changes in ownership, and decisions affecting contractual rights.

Build outbound lists from the asset's demonstrated commercial use rather than broad industry labels. Track a specific buyer problem, a plausible budget owner, and a reporting-capability hypothesis for every account before initiating contact.

Instrument workflow failures and commercial conversion separately. A successful file import is not a collected royalty, and a positive reply is not an executed license. Use stage definitions tied to documents, meetings, signatures, and cash.

Test fallback procedures with a missed report, duplicate event, revoked credential, and disputed renewal date. Confirm that the operator can reconstruct the current state and meet contractual deadlines without relying on the automation vendor's availability.

fields.name: Systems map and authoritative records
fields.prompt: Assign authoritative systems for contracts, assets, obligations, royalty calculations, receivables, and prospect stages. Document integration boundaries and prevent multiple applications from silently maintaining conflicting versions of the same commercial term.
fields.example: Executed agreements reside in restricted SharePoint storage; Airtable tracks obligations; QuickBooks records invoices and receipts; HubSpot tracks prospects. A versioned royalty ledger stores approved formulas. Contract amendments update the obligation register through a documented review, not by scraping a sales note or trusting the latest spreadsheet attachment.

fields.name: Royalty reporting automation specification
fields.prompt: Define ingestion triggers, schema validation, calculation versions, review queues, and statement release conditions. Show how the workflow handles repeated submissions and fails safely when required source data or contractual parameters are absent.
fields.example: A quarterly upload triggers CSV validation and computes royalties using formula version ROY-005. The event key combines licensee, period, and source checksum. Repeated uploads do not create duplicate invoices. Missing territory or currency values place the report in an exception queue; only reviewed statements synchronize with QuickBooks.

fields.name: Renewal alerts and notice verification
fields.prompt: Translate contract-specific renewal and termination notice periods into reminders with confirmed recipients and escalation. Distinguish internal planning alerts from legally effective notices and preserve proof of required delivery.
fields.example: A license expires December 31 and requires nonrenewal notice at least 90 days earlier. The system creates internal reviews 150, 120, and 105 days before expiry. The operator verifies the contractual counting rule and notice method, then records delivery evidence; an email reminder alone never constitutes the counterparty notice.

fields.name: Obligation tracking and change control
fields.prompt: Specify how new agreements and amendments create or change operational tasks. Require a comparison between the executed language and stored parameters before automated rates, deadlines, or access permissions change.
fields.example: Amendment AMD-002 expands territory to Canada on July 1 but leaves the 5% rate unchanged. A reviewer compares the signed document with the proposed parameter update. The ledger preserves earlier territory rules for historical periods and creates new delivery and reporting tasks only from the effective date.

fields.name: Ideal licensee list and outbound proposition
fields.prompt: Define a tightly bounded buyer segment, observable qualification signals, contact roles, and a proposition supported by asset evidence. Set a manageable outreach batch size that permits individual review and suppression checks.
fields.example: The first list contains 40 commercial refrigeration publishers and manufacturers with active manual-production teams. Each account record names a product-documentation leader and procurement contact. The message offers a 12-image evaluation addressing maintenance-diagram backlog, rather than a generic portfolio pitch. Suppressed contacts are excluded before each send.

fields.name: Growth stages and conversion economics
fields.prompt: Define measurable pipeline stages and conversion assumptions. Calculate acquisition cost using attributable spend, and keep expected licenses separate from signed contracts and recognized revenue when interpreting campaign results.
fields.example: A planning funnel uses 40 researched accounts, 12 replies, six qualified meetings, three paid evaluations, and one eventual license. With $4,000 attributable research and selling costs, modeled acquisition cost is $4,000 per signed license. Until that signature occurs, the figure remains a hypothesis rather than a realized conversion metric.

fields.name: Credential scope and data minimization
fields.prompt: Limit automation identities to the records and actions needed for their function. Specify secret storage, rotation, logging, export restrictions, and separation between prospect information and licensee transaction data.
fields.example: The reporting service can read its designated S3 prefix and write draft ledger records, but cannot delete source files or issue refunds. Credentials live in AWS Secrets Manager with access logging. HubSpot receives account status and renewal dates, not transaction-level sales exports or dataset source records.

fields.name: Underreporting and dispute fallback
fields.prompt: Define signals suggesting incomplete reporting and the bounded response to each signal. Separate anomaly detection from accusations, and preserve contractual rights while investigating source records and calculation differences.
fields.example: A 35% drop in reported royalties alongside unchanged shipment volumes triggers analyst review. The operator requests SKU-level reconciliation and affiliate-transfer records within the contract's response period. Undisputed amounts remain collectible. If the variance persists, the operator invokes the agreed audit process instead of automatically disabling all licensed operations.

fields.name: Outage recovery and manual operating packet
fields.prompt: Prepare a manual procedure for vendor outages, failed integrations, or corrupted imports. List available backups, responsible operators, reconciliation steps, and tests proving restored automation will not duplicate prior actions.
fields.example: The weekly recovery packet contains current contracts, obligation exports, open receivables, and approved calculation templates. During a 48-hour outage, the analyst prepares statements offline and records unique statement IDs. After restoration, a comparison of IDs and bank receipts prevents duplicate invoices and duplicate minimum-credit applications.

fields.name: Automation value and escalation thresholds
fields.prompt: Measure saved processing time, exception rates, statement accuracy, and deadline performance against a documented manual baseline. Set thresholds that require corrective work before adding more accounts or broader automation permissions.
fields.example: Four quarterly statements take eight analyst hours manually. The target workflow reduces that to three hours including review, saving five hours per cycle. Any duplicate invoice, missed notice deadline, or unexplained royalty difference above $100 pauses expansion until the operator fixes and retests the specific failure.

worksheets.completion_gate: The operator demonstrates one successful reporting cycle, one renewal notice check, and one manual recovery exercise; outbound stages and automation metrics remain separate from booked and collected revenue.

worksheets.title: 30-Day Launch Sprint, Pod Scorecard, and Exit Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Turn the licensing thesis into a disciplined first-month execution plan without compressing a 6-to-24-month sales cycle into an artificial promise. Assign pod responsibilities, track evidence-based milestones, preserve canonical economics, and assemble records that support renewal, delegation, and eventual transfer.
instructions: Treat the first 30 days as a preparation and validation sprint, not a requirement to close a license. Prioritize rights evidence, buyer qualification, contract economics, and a reproducible reporting demonstration over presentation volume or speculative revenue announcements.

Assign the Conservative and Base pod as one full-time operator plus three contractors. Define contractor deliverables and availability explicitly. Use the Scaled structure of two full-time staff plus four contractors only with a documented workload and cost reconciliation.

Review weekly leading indicators alongside cash and risk exposure. Separate researched prospects, qualified meetings, paid evaluations, signed grants, earned royalties, and collected receipts. A growing pipeline does not justify ignoring unresolved title or an approaching liquidity shortfall.

Build transfer readiness from the first contract. Retain assignments, amendments, reporting history, renewal dates, dispute records, and documented operating procedures. Flag assignment restrictions and buyer dependencies before estimating value from recurring royalties or marketing the portfolio.

At day 30, compare completed evidence with the original spending limits and rejection criteria. Choose continue, narrow, or stop for each opportunity. Authorize the next bounded work period only after updating cash, unresolved risks, and accountable owners.

fields.name: Days 1–7 rights and demand foundation
fields.prompt: Schedule the first week's asset intake, ownership review, buyer research, and capital setup. Assign concrete evidence deliverables and spending limits rather than activity counts without commercial or rights-validation value.
fields.example: By day seven, the operator creates the asset register, collects eight creator agreements, identifies 12 incomplete-title illustrations, and researches 40 target accounts. The rights contractor delivers a gap memo capped at $4,000. The cash ledger records $75,000 starting capital and separates committed setup costs from discretionary spending.

fields.name: Days 8–14 commercial and contract design
fields.prompt: Define second-week buyer interviews, sample evaluation design, royalty terms, and contract drafting outputs. Require confirmation of budget authority and reporting capability before treating an account as commercially qualified.
fields.example: By day fourteen, six discovery meetings identify three plausible evaluation candidates. The draft term sheet proposes $31,250 nonrecoupable fees, a 5% royalty, and a $60,000 annual minimum per Base-style account. Two buyers provide sample sales exports; procurement confirms the signatory path before negotiation costs expand.

fields.name: Days 15–21 reporting and delivery rehearsal
fields.prompt: Plan the third-week technical rehearsal using representative records and a bounded asset package. Specify calculation tests, exception handling, access checks, and the evidence required to demonstrate operational readiness without live contract execution.
fields.example: The analyst rehearses a $1,500,000 portfolio quarter, calculates $75,000 royalties, applies $60,000 minimum credits, and produces $15,000 additional royalties due. A duplicate invoice and unsupported deduction must fail. The delivery contractor validates 228 asset hashes and demonstrates access withdrawal on a test account.

fields.name: Days 22–30 evaluation and next-period decision
fields.prompt: Set final-week deliverables for buyer follow-up, risk closure, cash review, and operating handoff. State what evidence supports continued investment and which unresolved conditions require narrowing or stopping the opportunity.
fields.example: By day thirty, the operator has two qualified evaluation discussions, a reviewed term sheet, a reproducible royalty model, and a rights exception log. No license is signed. The decision authorizes another $6,000 of bounded work only if the liquidity forecast preserves the $16,000 buffer and buyer reporting tests succeed.

fields.name: Pod roles, capacity, and escalation ownership
fields.prompt: Assign accountable owners for commercial negotiation, rights review, royalty accounting, and delivery automation. Distinguish headcount from contractor hours, and document who can resolve disputed terms or authorize contractual actions.
fields.example: The Base pod has one full-time operator and three contractors: rights specialist, royalty accountant, and delivery engineer. The operator owns negotiation and notices; contractors provide bounded specialist deliverables. Scaled adds one full-time relationship manager and one audit contractor, reaching two full-time staff plus four contractors, six people total.

fields.name: Weekly operating and risk KPI scorecard
fields.prompt: Define each metric with a denominator, source system, review frequency, and response threshold. Include rights coverage, buyer qualification, report timeliness, reconciliation accuracy, collection exposure, and minimum cash rather than revenue alone.
fields.example: The weekly scorecard shows 228 of 240 assets cleared, two of six meetings commercially qualified, and four of four test statements reconciled. Required live statement timeliness is 100%. Any receivable over 30 days past due receives an owner; forecast unrestricted cash below $16,000 triggers a spending review.

fields.name: Canonical economics and leverage checkpoint
fields.prompt: Restate the canonical portfolio economics and leverage rating without changing them to match an early pipeline. Explain how actual contracts and costs will be compared with these reference scenarios over time.
fields.example: Candidate 19 ranks 13 of 29 with a 88/100 score: revenue potential 24, margin potential 24, team efficiency 19, startup accessibility 11, and automation potential 10. Annual revenue and owner net remain $50,000/$12,500 Conservative, $425,000/$180,625 Base, and $800,000/$480,000 Scaled. The score expresses operating leverage, not a probability of closing or a substitute for deal underwriting.

fields.name: Renewal quality and concentration exposure
fields.prompt: Measure renewal eligibility, payment performance, licensee concentration, remaining term, and dependence on specific assets. Separate recurring contractual economics from nonrecurring fees when judging the durability of future cash flows.
fields.example: Four equal Base accounts each contribute $106,250 first-year revenue, creating 25% concentration per account. Their combined $125,000 fees do not automatically repeat at renewal. The renewal forecast separately models $300,000 earned royalties at current sales, $240,000 contractual minimums if renewed, and any new fees only when supported by specific renewal terms.

fields.name: Exit-readiness evidence and transfer restrictions
fields.prompt: Build the record set a purchaser would need to validate ownership, transferability, cash generation, and operational continuity. Flag required consents, unresolved claims, and personal relationships that cannot transfer through document delivery alone.
fields.example: The exit folder contains assignments, executed licenses, amendments, 24 months of statements when accumulated, bank reconciliations, audit findings, renewal schedules, and operating procedures. Two agreements require counterparty consent for assignment. Those dependencies remain explicit in the transfer ledger; the operator does not present the portfolio as freely transferable before resolving them.

fields.name: Day-30 decision and next 90-day mandate
fields.prompt: Record completed evidence, actual spend, remaining cash, unresolved risks, and the next bounded mandate. Choose an explicit continue, narrow, or stop decision without treating unsigned pipeline as achieved revenue or promised collections.
fields.example: Decision: continue with the 228 cleared catalog assets and exclude the 12 defective-title items. The first month spends $9,000 underwriting and $8,000 fixed overhead from $75,000, leaving $58,000 before other committed setup payments. The next 90 days target three qualified evaluations and one negotiated draft; first-deal timing remains 6 to 24 months.

worksheets.completion_gate: The operator signs the day-30 decision with actual spending, cash, evidence, pod ownership, and the next bounded mandate; canonical scenario figures and transfer restrictions remain intact in the record.
